name: Dark blue slate
lede: Dark blue slate is a muted, bluish-grey modifier on [[blue-slate]], scanned from Ridgway's 1912 plates and filed by the ISCC-NBS system in 1955, and is an exact color match for a separately named [[dark-blue-slate|Dark Violet-Slate]].

sections.title: Two catalogue names, one color
sections.body:
The name follows the library's modifier grammar, *dark* plus [[blue-slate]], and both Ridgway's 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* and the ISCC-NBS system of 1955 cite a block this dark and muted, without naming a plate number for this particular chip [1]. Our library finds that Dark Violet-Slate, from a separate source, measures to the identical hex value, close enough that the two names describe the same chip under different catalogues [1]. The books do not explain the choice of "dark" over another modifier [2].

Its nearest named neighbors are [[dark-violet-grey]] and [[dark-payne-s-grey]], both almost indistinguishable at 3.1 to 3.3 units [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: A color this close to Dark blue slate is common in our archive: 501 of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, about 2.1 percent, more common than 70 percent of the named colors [4]. It is most often a shadow, 36 percent of the time, and is most overrepresented in paintings from India, at 2.4 times expected [4]. The earliest match dates to 1100, 812 years before the name's earliest record [4]. That is centuries before the name's own record, a floor on the hue's age, not a first use of either the name or a pigment.
